profile.summary: hgT5 is a set of T5 transformer models pretrained on the human genome by the authors of the GUANinE benchmark. The models read DNA sequences of about 512 bp, split into learned tokens, and were fine-tuned separately on each GUANinE task, such as chromatin accessibility, sequence conservation and yeast promoter expression. They were built to test how self-supervised pretraining helps on these tasks.
profile.summary_source_locator: GUANinE v1.0: Abstract; section 3.3 Novel Neural Baselines; Appendix E

summary_quotes.text: hgT5-515, -2051, -8195 These models are identical to the T5-515, -2051, and -8195 above except that they undergo self-supervised pretraining on a repeat-downsampled subset of hg38 (1.64 Gbp) before fine-tuning.
All T5 models and pretrained hgT5 models were finetuned on each task separately
Note the T5 and hgT5-8195 use ≤ 512 bp of input sequence.
the GUANinE benchmark allows us to evaluate new self-supervised T5 models and explore the tradeoffs between tokenization and model performance

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: hgT5 uses the T5 encoder-decoder transformer at 770 M parameters. DNA is split into tokens with a unigram language model tokenizer, with vocabularies of 512+3, 2048+3 or 8192+3 tokens. The models were pretrained on the human genome with T5's span-corruption objective, using 15% noise density and a mean span length of 3 tokens, then fine-tuned on each benchmark task separately. Matching T5 models without pretraining were trained as a comparison.

quotes.text: We also train large (770 M parameter) transformers on each task
We use the text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) architecture, an encoder-decoder transformer designed for efficient self-supervised pretraining and transfer learning
These models correspond to a T5 architecture with tokenized inputs via a unigram language model [42]. The vocabulary sizes evaluated are 512+3, 2048+3, and 8192+3 tokens
Self-supervised pretraining was done with a 15% noise density and mean span length of 3 tokens.
the T5 utilizes a more efficient span-corruption task for language modeling

sections.title: Pretraining corpus
sections.body: The pretraining corpus is a reduced copy of hg38. The authors removed N-rich and repeat-rich regions and near-duplicate segments, which left 1.64 Gbp. They then made upsampled versions in which minor alleles from 1000 Genomes Project Phase 3 (allele frequency 1e-3 or greater) were inserted at random, to reduce reference bias.

quotes.text: we took the approach of narrowing down the human genome by first removing N-rich sequences
These procedures left us with 1.64 Gbp of genomic sequence before augmentation.
we obtained genetic variants from unrelated individuals in the 1000 Genomes Project Phase 3 [68] with an allele frequency of 1e-3 or greater
2. reduce reference bias introduced by training on the reference genome;

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Three hgT5 models exist, named by vocabulary size: hgT5-515, hgT5-2051 and hgT5-8195. The authors trained three pretraining replicates of each and kept two. Each was then fine-tuned per task, so a published score refers to a task-specific fine-tuned model. GUANinE v1.1 re-reports hgT5-8195. The README says the T5 baseline models are still being converted, and the Hugging Face ID in its example did not resolve on 2026-11-26, so a result cannot yet name a public checkpoint.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: DNA language model: a T5 encoder-decoder pretrained with span corruption on the human genome, then fine-tuned per task.

quotes.text: Pretraining with self-supervised language modeling (span corruption) has a strong, positive impact on T5 performance in our benchmark

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: T5 (text-to-text transfer transformer), an encoder-decoder transformer, with unigram language model tokenisation of DNA.

quotes.text: We use the text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) architecture, an encoder-decoder transformer
with tokenized inputs via a unigram language model

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: DNA sequence, tokenised into segments of up to 512 tokens. On GUANinE tasks the input is at most 512 bp.
facts.source_locator: GUANinE v1.0: Figure 1 caption; Appendix D

quotes.text: use tokenization to increase our context length within 512-token segments
Note the T5 and hgT5-8195 use ≤ 512 bp of input sequence.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: After fine-tuning, a task prediction produced by the T5 decoder as text tokens, for example a regression value from an output vocabulary. The pretrained model's own output is span-corruption predictions.
facts.source_locator: README.md: Baseline Model Usage; GUANinE v1.0: section 5.3

facts.label: Parameters

strengths.text: The pretraining corpus is designed to reduce repeats and reference bias: repeat-rich and duplicated regions are removed and common human variants are added.

quotes.text: our hg38 pretraining corpus is repeat-downsampled [44] and contains significant human variation [68], which may improve its utility

strengths.text: The same T5 models were trained with and without pretraining, so the effect of pretraining can be read directly. The authors report that pretraining improved scores without extra sequence context; this is their own result.

quotes.text: pretraining strongly improves performance as well — notably, this improvement is obtained without additional sequence context, in contrast to other pretrained models

strengths.text: Three tokenizer sizes are compared, which shows the trade-off between tokenisation and performance.

quotes.text: On GPRA tasks, the loss incurred by tokenization (i.e. T5 vs T5-515, etc) is largely offset by pretraining

limitations.text: Public weights could not be confirmed. The README says the models are still being converted, and the Hugging Face ID in its example did not resolve.

no_run_guide_reason: No public hgT5 checkpoint could be found. The README example loads guanine/t5_baseline and names no hgT5 checkpoint; that Hugging Face ID returned an error on 2026-11-26, and the README says the T5 models are still being converted.
notes: hgT5 comes from the GUANinE v1.0 paper (Robson and Ioannidis, PMLR v240), which is the model's own source; the existing record source (GUANinE v1.1) only re-reports hgT5-8195. The record covers three variants (hgT5-515, -2051, -8195). The Hugging Face organisation 'guanine' lists datasets but no models via the public API. The v1.0 PDF is quoted from its pdftotext text layer; its licence is not stated, so store_bytes is false. The README and docs are EUPL-1.2 code-repository files and are not CC BY, so store_bytes is false for them; change this if EUPL redistribution is acceptable.
